claim: PDAC remains associated with poor long-term survival.
source: Therapeutic control of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the greatest challenges in oncology and PDAC remains associated with poor long-term survival (Arnold et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Arnold et al., 2019.

claim: Immunotherapy has transformed the clinical outlook for many tumor subtypes.
source: Although immunotherapy has transformed the clinical outlook for many tumor subtypes its impact on PDAC has been disappointing to date.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about immunotherapy in oncology.

claim: The impact of immunotherapy on PDAC has been disappointing to date.
source: Although immunotherapy has transformed the clinical outlook for many tumor subtypes its impact on PDAC has been disappointing to date.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about PDAC treatment.

claim: The PDAC microenvironment is associated with an intense desmoplastic reaction characterized by an abundance of cancer associated fibroblasts.
source: One factor in this regard may be the characteristic nature of the PDAC microenvironment which is associated with an intense desmoplastic reaction characterized by an abundance of cancer associated fibroblasts (CAF; Biffi and Tuveson, 2021; Menezes et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Biffi and Tuveson, 2021 and Menezes et al., 2022.

claim: Fibroblasts are key regulators of tumor biology.
source: Fibroblasts are key regulators of tumor biology and there is now intense interest in understanding how they may act to maintain or suppress tumor growth.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about fibroblasts in cancer.

claim: CAF are the predominant source of extracellular matrix.
source: CAF are the predominant source of extracellular matrix and develop a complex system of interactions with tumor cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about CAF function.

claim: CAF develop a complex system of interactions with tumor cells.
source: CAF are the predominant source of extracellular matrix and develop a complex system of interactions with tumor cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about CAF function.

claim: CAF differ from normal counterparts by relative resistance to apoptosis or reversion of quiescence.
source: Although some of the characteristics of CAF suggest chronic activation with sustained production of alpha-small muscle actin(α-SMA), they differ from normal counterparts by relative resistance to apoptosis or reversion of quiescence (Piersma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Piersma et al., 2020.

claim: PDAC-associated CAF can limit the access of immune effector cells to tumor.
source: PDAC-associated CAF can limit the access of immune effector cells to tumor (Mhaidly and Mechta-Grigoriou, 2021; Inoue et al., 2016; Ene-Obong et al., 2013), promote the infiltration of immune suppressive leucocyte populations and directly support tumor growth (Kumar et al., 2017; Albrengues et al., 2014; Mezawa and Orimo, 2016; Fang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mhaidly and Mechta-Grigoriou, 2021; Inoue et al., 2016; Ene-Obong et al., 2013.

claim: PDAC-associated CAF promote the infiltration of immune suppressive leucocyte populations.
source: PDAC-associated CAF can limit the access of immune effector cells to tumor (Mhaidly and Mechta-Grigoriou, 2021; Inoue et al., 2016; Ene-Obong et al., 2013), promote the infiltration of immune suppressive leucocyte populations and directly support tumor growth (Kumar et al., 2017; Albrengues et al., 2014; Mezawa and Orimo, 2016; Fang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kumar et al., 2017; Albrengues et al., 2014; Mezawa and Orimo, 2016; Fang et al., 2019.

claim: PDAC-associated CAF directly support tumor growth.
source: PDAC-associated CAF can limit the access of immune effector cells to tumor (Mhaidly and Mechta-Grigoriou, 2021; Inoue et al., 2016; Ene-Obong et al., 2013), promote the infiltration of immune suppressive leucocyte populations and directly support tumor growth (Kumar et al., 2017; Albrengues et al., 2014; Mezawa and Orimo, 2016; Fang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kumar et al., 2017; Albrengues et al., 2014; Mezawa and Orimo, 2016; Fang et al., 2019.

claim: Fibroblasts may play a protective role in limiting tumor metastasis.
source: However, studies from murine models have also shown that fibroblasts may also play a protective role in limiting tumor metastasis and that targeting of stromal cells can accelerate disease progression (Özdemir et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Özdemir et al., 2014.

claim: Targeting of stromal cells can accelerate disease progression.
source: However, studies from murine models have also shown that fibroblasts may also play a protective role in limiting tumor metastasis and that targeting of stromal cells can accelerate disease progression (Özdemir et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Özdemir et al., 2014.

claim: A clinical trial that targeted CAF through inhibition of the hedgehog protein, combined with chemotherapy, was terminated early due to disease progression.
source: Furthermore, a clinical trial that targeted CAF through inhibition of the hedgehog protein, combined with chemotherapy, was terminated early due to disease progression (Catenacci et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Catenacci et al., 2015.

claim: Transcriptional analyses have shown at least four subsets of CAF in PDAC with a heterogenous profile and direct associations with clinical outcome.
source: Transcriptional analyses have shown at least four subsets of CAF in PDAC with a heterogenous profile and direct associations with clinical outcome (Mezawa and Orimo, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mezawa and Orimo, 2016.

claim: α-SMAhigh myofibroblast populations are closely associated with tumor whilst inflammatory subsets reside more distally.
source: Spatially related features are also observed with α-SMAhigh myofibroblast populations closely associated with tumor whilst inflammatory subsets reside more distally (Öhlund et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Öhlund et al., 2017.

claim: Cytokines such as TGF and IL-1 appear as key regulators and may direct differentiation from a CD105 +precursor.
source: Cytokines such as TGF and IL-1 appear as key regulators and may direct differentiation from a CD105 +precursor (Dominguez et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dominguez et al., 2020.

claim: Marked cellular plasticity is a feature of CAF.
source: Marked cellular plasticity is a feature of CAF (Neuzillet et al., 2019), although it remains unclear if CAF develop discrete lineages or are interchangeable.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Neuzillet et al., 2019.

claim: A population of LRRC15+ myofibroblasts is emerging as a potential tumor-associated subset with direct impact on clinical responses to therapy within PDAC.
source: Within PDAC a population of LRRC15+ myofibroblasts is emerging as a potential tumor-associated subset with direct impact on clinical responses to therapy (Dominguez et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dominguez et al., 2020.

claim: Histological slide sections were obtained from tumor biopsies of 24 patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma who had undergone surgical resection for localized disease.
source: Histological slide sections were obtained from tumor biopsies of 24 patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) who had undergone surgical resection for localized disease.
evidence: This describes the study cohort and methods.

claim: Thirteen patients had died of PDAC within 12 months of diagnosis.
source: Thirteen patients had died of PDAC within 12 months of diagnosis (subsequently referred to as 'poor response') whilst 11 had survived for at least 36 months ('good response').
evidence: This describes the study cohort characteristics.

claim: Eleven patients had survived for at least 36 months.
source: Thirteen patients had died of PDAC within 12 months of diagnosis (subsequently referred to as 'poor response') whilst 11 had survived for at least 36 months ('good response').
evidence: This describes the study cohort characteristics.

claim: Four-plex immunofluorescence staining was used to define major anatomical subregions of the tumor.
source: Four-plex immunofluorescence staining was used initially to define major anatomical subregions of the tumor.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Antibodies against pan-cytokeratin, α-SMA and CD45 identified epithelial, fibroblast and immune populations respectively.
source: Antibodies against pan-cytokeratin, α-SMA and CD45 identified epithelial, fibroblast and immune populations respectively whilst DAPI staining defined nuclear architecture.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: DAPI staining defined nuclear architecture.
source: Antibodies against pan-cytokeratin, α-SMA and CD45 identified epithelial, fibroblast and immune populations respectively whilst DAPI staining defined nuclear architecture.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Four regions of interest within each of three domains were selected from each patient for assessment using the NanoString GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler platform.
source: Regions in which stromal cells were adjacent to tumor ('tumor-proximal stroma'), distant from tumor ('tumor-distal stroma') or enriched for CD45+ immune cells ('immune enriched') were then selected and 4 areas ('regions of interest'; ROI) within each of these 3 domains were selected from each patient for assessment using the NanoString GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler (DSP) platform (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the methodology and is illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Ninety-four RNA hybridization probes for 81 endogenous, 6 housekeeping and 7 negative control genes were applied to the 12 ROI from each patient, generating 288 transcriptional datasets.
source: Ninety-four RNA hybridization probes (Supplementary file 1, Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2) for 81 endogenous, 6 housekeeping and 7 negative control genes were then applied to the 12 ROI from each patient, thus generating 288 transcriptional datasets.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of transcriptional datasets delineated immune and stromal regions.
source: Hierarchical clustering of transcriptional datasets delineated immune and stromal regions with two immune profiles clustering separately due to differential expression of activatory and inhibitory immune genes.
evidence: This describes the results of data analysis.

claim: Two immune profiles clustered separately due to differential expression of activatory and inhibitory immune genes.
source: Hierarchical clustering of transcriptional datasets delineated immune and stromal regions with two immune profiles clustering separately due to differential expression of activatory and inhibitory immune genes.
evidence: This describes the results of data analysis.

claim: Cell-type expression profiles were consistent with immune or stromal origin.
source: Cell-type expression profiles were consistent with immune or stromal origin (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: UMAP analysis broadly separated tumor, proximal stroma, distal stroma, and immune regions.
source: UMAP analysis broadly separated tumor, proximal stroma, distal stroma, and immune regions (Figure 2B), although overlay of clinical outcome data did not reveal significant clustering.
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Overlay of clinical outcome data did not reveal significant clustering.
source: UMAP analysis broadly separated tumor, proximal stroma, distal stroma, and immune regions (Figure 2B), although overlay of clinical outcome data did not reveal significant clustering.
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Monocyte representation was equivalent within stromal and immune regions, consistent with broad infiltration within PDAC microenvironment.
source: These confirmed localization of epithelial, fibroblast and lymphoid cells within the tumor, stromal and immune regions respectively whilst monocyte representation was equivalent within stromal and immune regions, consistent with broad infiltration within PDAC microenvironment.
evidence: This describes the results of cell lineage marker analysis.

claim: CD3E and MS4A1 expression indicated that stromal regions also contained smaller populations of infiltrating T and B cells.
source: CD3E and MS4A1 expression indicated that stromal regions also contained smaller populations of infiltrating T and B cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Stromal regions expressed canonical fibroblast markers such as THY1, PDPN, and FAP.
source: Stromal regions expressed canonical fibroblast markers such as THY1, PDPN, and FAP whilst immune-specific genes such as PTPRC, CD3E and MS4A1 were present within Immune regions (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 2D, E, and supplement 4.

claim: Immune-specific genes such as PTPRC, CD3E and MS4A1 were present within Immune regions.
source: Stromal regions expressed canonical fibroblast markers such as THY1, PDPN, and FAP whilst immune-specific genes such as PTPRC, CD3E and MS4A1 were present within Immune regions (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 2D, E, and supplement 4.

claim: The great majority of stromal-associated genes were expressed from fibroblasts.
source: This revealed that, whilst the great majority of stromal-associated genes were expressed from fibroblasts, the expression of CSF1R within stroma was largely derived from myeloid cells, CTNNB1 localized to endothelial cells and expression of KRT was identified as KRT18 within epithelial cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This describes the results of mapping to scRNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2 supplement 5C.

claim: The expression of CSF1R within stroma was largely derived from myeloid cells.
source: This revealed that, whilst the great majority of stromal-associated genes were expressed from fibroblasts, the expression of CSF1R within stroma was largely derived from myeloid cells, CTNNB1 localized to endothelial cells and expression of KRT was identified as KRT18 within epithelial cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This describes the results of mapping to scRNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2 supplement 5C.

claim: CTNNB1 localized to endothelial cells.
source: This revealed that, whilst the great majority of stromal-associated genes were expressed from fibroblasts, the expression of CSF1R within stroma was largely derived from myeloid cells, CTNNB1 localized to endothelial cells and expression of KRT was identified as KRT18 within epithelial cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This describes the results of mapping to scRNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2 supplement 5C.

claim: Expression of KRT was identified as KRT18 within epithelial cells.
source: This revealed that, whilst the great majority of stromal-associated genes were expressed from fibroblasts, the expression of CSF1R within stroma was largely derived from myeloid cells, CTNNB1 localized to endothelial cells and expression of KRT was identified as KRT18 within epithelial cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This describes the results of mapping to scRNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2 supplement 5C.

claim: Transcriptional profiles varied markedly between tumor-proximal or tumor-distal ROI.
source: Transcriptional profiles were seen to vary markedly between tumor-proximal or tumor-distal ROI.
evidence: This describes the results of comparing proximal and distal stroma.

claim: Expression of DKK3 was markedly increased in stroma-proximal regions.
source: In particular, expression of DKK3 and PDPN was markedly increased in stroma-proximal regions (Figure 3A, B and C) and both are established markers of cancer-associated fibroblasts implicated in support of tumor growth (Zhou et al., 2018; Hirayama et al., 2018; Shindo et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 3A, B, and C, supported by citations.

claim: Expression of PDPN was markedly increased in stroma-proximal regions.
source: In particular, expression of DKK3 and PDPN was markedly increased in stroma-proximal regions (Figure 3A, B and C) and both are established markers of cancer-associated fibroblasts implicated in support of tumor growth (Zhou et al., 2018; Hirayama et al., 2018; Shindo et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 3A, B, and C, supported by citations.

claim: DKK3 and PDPN are established markers of cancer-associated fibroblasts implicated in support of tumor growth.
source: In particular, expression of DKK3 and PDPN was markedly increased in stroma-proximal regions (Figure 3A, B and C) and both are established markers of cancer-associated fibroblasts implicated in support of tumor growth (Zhou et al., 2018; Hirayama et al., 2018; Shindo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhou et al., 2018; Hirayama et al., 2018; Shindo et al., 2013.

claim: Expression of C3, SFRP2, STAT3, IL-6 and THY1 was increased in tumor-distal stroma.
source: In contrast, expression of C3, SFRP2, STAT3, IL-6 and THY1 was increased in tumor-distal stroma.

claim: C3 and SFRP2 expression were particularly elevated in tumor-distal stroma.
source: C3 and SFRP2 expression were particularly elevated (Figure 3C) and localization of C3 expression to fibroblasts was further suggested by correlation with fibroblast, but not monocyte, marker genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 3C and supplement 1.

claim: Localization of C3 expression to fibroblasts was suggested by correlation with fibroblast, but not monocyte, marker genes.
source: C3 and SFRP2 expression were particularly elevated (Figure 3C) and localization of C3 expression to fibroblasts was further suggested by correlation with fibroblast, but not monocyte, marker genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 3 supplement 1.

claim: SFRP2 acts as a Wnt inhibitor.
source: This is noteworthy given the emerging importance for intracellular complement expression and the action of SFRP2 as a Wnt inhibitor.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about SFRP2 function.

claim: THY1 is commonly expressed on stem-like populations of fibroblasts.
source: STAT3 and IL-6 expression could be explained by their presence within inflammatory CAFs whilst THY1 is commonly expressed on stem-like populations of fibroblasts (Shi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shi et al., 2019.

claim: The stem cell marker CD34 was expressed in tumor-distal regions.
source: The stem cell marker CD34 was also expressed in this region (Figure 3A, B and C).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 3A, B, and C.

claim: Immunohistochemical staining confirmed extreme polarization of podoplanin, DKK3 and C3 expression in relation to tumor proximity.
source: Immunohistochemical staining confirmed extreme polarization of podoplanin, DKK3 and C3 expression in relation to tumor proximity.
evidence: This describes the results of immunohistochemical validation.

claim: Podoplanin was expressed on stroma that encased tumor.
source: Podoplanin was expressed on stroma that encased tumor whilst DKK3 expression was present both within tumor and tumor-proximal stroma.
evidence: This describes the results of immunohistochemical staining.

claim: DKK3 expression was present both within tumor and tumor-proximal stroma.
source: Podoplanin was expressed on stroma that encased tumor whilst DKK3 expression was present both within tumor and tumor-proximal stroma.
evidence: This describes the results of immunohistochemical staining.

claim: Expression of C3 was localized to distal stroma regions.
source: In contrast, expression of C3 was localized to distal stroma regions (Figure 3D).

claim: Two fibroblast clusters were observed from scRNA-Seq unsupervised clustering analysis and defined as sc-proximal and sc-distal populations.
source: Two fibroblast clusters were observed from scRNA-Seq unsupervised clustering analysis and defined as sc-proximal and sc-distal populations due to their distinct proximal and distant gene expression signatures (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Transcriptional profiles were highly divergent between proximal compared to distal clusters with 47 genes differentially upregulated in the distal cluster and 36 genes differentially upregulated in the proximal cluster.
source: Transcriptional profiles were highly divergent between proximal compared to distal clusters with 47 genes differentially upregulated in the distal cluster and 36 genes differentially upregulated in the proximal cluster (Figure 4D).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The sc-proximal clusters showed high expression of myofibroblast (myCAF) marker genes including MMP11 and HOPX.
source: The sc-proximal clusters showed high expression of myofibroblast (myCAF) marker genes including MMP11 and HOPX whilst the distal population was enriched for expression of genes associated with inflammatory CAF (iCAF) such as CXCL12 and CFD (Figure 4E).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The distal population was enriched for expression of genes associated with inflammatory CAF (iCAF) such as CXCL12 and CFD.
source: The sc-proximal clusters showed high expression of myofibroblast (myCAF) marker genes including MMP11 and HOPX whilst the distal population was enriched for expression of genes associated with inflammatory CAF (iCAF) such as CXCL12 and CFD (Figure 4E).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Sc-proximal fibroblasts are enriched for cell division, chemotaxis and heat shock protein binding.
source: This showed that sc-proximal fibroblasts are enriched for cell division, chemotaxis and heat shock protein binding.
evidence: This describes the results of pathway enrichment analysis.

claim: Sc-proximal fibroblasts express a wide range of Wnt ligands including WNT5A, WNT11, WNT2, WNT5, WNT5A and WNT5B.
source: Furthermore, they express a wide range of Wnt ligands including WNT5A, WNT11, WNT2, WNT5, WNT5A and WNT5B (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: Sc-distal fibroblasts show enrichment of pathways associated with generation of the extracellular matrix, negative regulation of stem cell proliferation, complement activation and retinoic acid metabolism.
source: In contrast, sc-distal fibroblasts show enrichment of pathways associated with generation of the extracellular matrix, negative regulation of stem cell proliferation, complement activation and retinoic acid metabolism (Figure 4F).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 4F.

claim: High level transcriptional expression of PDPN, HIF1A, PDL1 (CD274), and VEGFA were associated with poor clinical outcome.
source: High level transcriptional expression of PDPN, HIF1A, PDL1 (CD274), and VEGFA were associated with poor clinical outcome (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).

claim: Ten genes were upregulated in patients with survival beyond 3 years and were characterized predominantly by immune activation with increased expression of MHC class I and class II, complement C3 and chemokines CCL5 and CXCL9.
source: Ten genes were upregulated in patients with survival beyond 3 years and were characterized predominantly by immune activation with increased expression of MHC class I and class II, complement C3 and chemokines CCL5 and CXCL9.
evidence: This describes the results of differential expression analysis by survival.

claim: The integrin ITGB2 (CD18) and STAT1 showed increased expression in patients with survival beyond 3 years.
source: The integrin ITGB2 (CD18) and STAT1 also showed increased expression in this group.
evidence: This describes the results of differential expression analysis by survival.

claim: Patients with a poor outcome expressed PDPN broadly across the tumor microenvironment.
source: Patients with a poor outcome expressed PDPN broadly across the tumor microenvironment whilst HIF-1α and VEGF expression also extended into the distal stromal and immune regions and likely indicates more extensive hypoxia in this subgroup.
evidence: This describes the results of spatial expression analysis by outcome.

claim: HIF-1α and VEGF expression extended into the distal stromal and immune regions in patients with poor outcome, likely indicating more extensive hypoxia in this subgroup.
source: Patients with a poor outcome expressed PDPN broadly across the tumor microenvironment whilst HIF-1α and VEGF expression also extended into the distal stromal and immune regions and likely indicates more extensive hypoxia in this subgroup.
evidence: This describes the results of spatial expression analysis by outcome and provides an interpretation.

claim: Good prognosis was associated with broad expression of most immunostimulatory and immunoregulatory genes.
source: Good prognosis was associated with broad expression of most immunostimulatory and immunoregulatory genes whilst expression of IL-11 and HLA-E was focused within distal stroma (Figure 5C, D and E).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 5C, D, and E.

claim: Expression of IL-11 and HLA-E was focused within distal stroma in patients with good prognosis.
source: Good prognosis was associated with broad expression of most immunostimulatory and immunoregulatory genes whilst expression of IL-11 and HLA-E was focused within distal stroma (Figure 5C, D and E).
evidence: This describes the results shown in Figure 5C, D, and E.

claim: Expression of complement C3 and NKG7 within the immune region was enhanced in patients with good clinical outcome.
source: Expression of complement C3 and NKG7, a regulator of cytotoxic granule release (Ng et al., 2020) within the immune region was also enhanced in patients with good clinical outcome.
evidence: This describes the results of spatial expression analysis by outcome, with citation for NKG7 function.

claim: NKG7 is a regulator of cytotoxic granule release.
source: Expression of complement C3 and NKG7, a regulator of cytotoxic granule release (Ng et al., 2020) within the immune region was also enhanced in patients with good clinical outcome.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ng et al., 2020.

claim: Proximity to tumor was seen to be a strong determinant of transcriptional activity of stromal cells.
source: Proximity to tumor was seen to be a strong determinant of transcriptional activity of stromal cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: PDPN expression is strongly enhanced on cancer-associated fibroblasts in PDAC.
source: PDPN expression is strongly enhanced on cancer-associated fibroblasts in PDAC (Shindo et al., 2013) and high expression levels are correlated with poor prognosis in some, but not all, studies (Mezawa and Orimo, 2016).

claim: High PDPN expression levels are correlated with poor prognosis in some, but not all, studies.
source: PDPN expression is strongly enhanced on cancer-associated fibroblasts in PDAC (Shindo et al., 2013) and high expression levels are correlated with poor prognosis in some, but not all, studies (Mezawa and Orimo, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mezawa and Orimo, 2016.

claim: DKK3 is a Wnt regulator and is emerging as a potentially important therapeutic target.
source: DKK3 is a Wnt regulator and is emerging as a potentially important therapeutic target (Zhou et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2018.

claim: CD34 is a marker of stromal stem cells.
source: CD34, a marker of stromal stem cells, was also expressed more highly in this region and may indicate spatial differentiation of stromal cells towards the tumor.

claim: Tumor-proximal populations displayed features typical of myofibroblasts whilst more distal populations had an inflammatory profile.
source: Tumor-proximal populations displayed features typical of myofibroblasts whilst more distal populations had an inflammatory profile, in line with previous reports (Öhlund et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Öhlund et al., 2017.

claim: Myofibroblast markers included the potent pro-tumorigenic chemokine CXCL14.
source: Myofibroblast markers included the potent pro-tumorigenic chemokine CXCL14 (Augsten et al., 2014) and WNT5A which may contribute to the differentiation of adipocytes to CAFs (Zoico et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Augsten et al., 2014.

claim: WNT5A may contribute to the differentiation of adipocytes to CAFs.
source: Myofibroblast markers included the potent pro-tumorigenic chemokine CXCL14 (Augsten et al., 2014) and WNT5A which may contribute to the differentiation of adipocytes to CAFs (Zoico et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zoico et al., 2016.

claim: Wnt ligand signaling plays a key role in PDAC progression and therapeutic resistance.

evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Wnt signaling in PDAC.

claim: Tumor-proximal fibroblasts are strong contributors to the Wnt ligand pool with high level expression of the ligands WNT5A, WNT11, WNT2, WNT5, WNT5A, and WNT5B.
source: Indeed, Wnt ligand signaling plays a key role in PDAC progression and therapeutic resistance, and tumor-proximal fibroblasts are seen to be strong contributors to the Wnt ligand pool with high level expression of the ligands WNT5A, WNT11, WNT2, WNT5, WNT5A, and WNT5B.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: Transcriptional regulation of cell division was increased in tumor-proximal fibroblasts, suggesting enhanced proliferation of stromal cells when locally exposed to tumor.
source: Transcriptional regulation of cell division was also increased, suggesting enhanced proliferation of stromal cells when locally exposed to tumor and in line with prior reports (Kalluri and Zeisberg, 2006).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, supported by a citation to Kalluri and Zeisberg, 2006.

claim: CAF populations expressing complement proteins have been observed previously in PDAC.
source: CAF populations expressing complement proteins have been observed previously in PDAC (Chen et al., 2021a) and overlap with the transcriptional profile of inflammatory CAF.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2021a.

claim: Intracellular complement expression may impact on immune surveillance in pre-clinical models.
